text: Lesson 13 introduced the Case object and its Status field. This lesson goes one level deeper: how a case actually moves through Status values, and what automation drives that movement.

Most Service Cloud orgs implement some version of the same lifecycle: New, then In Progress while a rep works it, possibly Escalated if it needs urgent attention, then Closed. The pattern is standard — the exact wording of each stage varies org to org, so never assume a Status value means the same thing everywhere.

Case Assignment Rules automatically route a new case to the right owner based on origin, priority, or product — instead of leaving it unassigned. Escalation Rules watch for cases open too long relative to their priority and automatically escalate them, reassigning or notifying a manager.

A rising count of escalated cases is often an early warning sign of a support team falling behind, well before total volume looks alarming. Next up: service cloud reporting context — the metrics an analyst actually reports on.
